article_title: Information to be provided where personal data are collected from the data subject

test_cases.question: When must a company provide privacy information to someone whose data it collects directly?
test_cases.answer: The information must be provided at the time when personal data are obtained from the data subject, not at some later date or upon request.
test_cases.supporting_quote: the controller shall, at the time when personal data are obtained, provide the data subject with all of the following information
key_phrases: at the time when personal data are obtained

test_cases.question: If a company obtains personal data from a third party rather than directly from the individual, do the information duties that attach to direct collection still apply?
test_cases.answer: No. Article 13 specifically applies only when personal data is collected from the data subject directly. When data is obtained from a source other than the data subject, different requirements under Article 14 would apply instead.
test_cases.supporting_quote: Where personal data relating to a data subject are collected from the data subject

test_cases.question: What contact details must a company provide about themselves when collecting personal data directly from individuals?
test_cases.answer: They must provide the identity and contact details of the controller and, where applicable, the contact details of the controller's representative and the data protection officer.
test_cases.supporting_quote: the identity and the contact details of the controller and, where applicable, of the controller's representative; the contact details of the data protection officer, where applicable

test_cases.question: What must a company tell people about how their data will be used when collecting it directly from them?
test_cases.answer: The company must provide the purposes of the processing for which the personal data are intended as well as the legal basis for the processing. If relying on legitimate interests, they must also specify what those legitimate interests are.
test_cases.supporting_quote: the purposes of the processing for which the personal data are intended as well as the legal basis for the processing; where the processing is based on point (f) of Article 6(1), the legitimate interests pursued by the controller or by a third party

test_cases.question: When is a company required to inform data subjects about transfers of their data to countries outside the EU?
test_cases.answer: Information about transfers of personal data to third countries or international organizations must be provided when such transfers are intended. This includes informing the data subject about the existence or absence of an adequacy decision, or the appropriate safeguards in place and how to obtain a copy of them.
test_cases.supporting_quote: where applicable, the fact that the controller intends to transfer personal data to a third country or international organisation and the existence or absence of an adequacy decision by the Commission, or... reference to the appropriate or suitable safeguards and the means by which to obtain a copy of them

test_cases.question: What additional information must be provided to ensure fair and transparent processing?
test_cases.answer: In addition to basic information, the controller must provide: the retention period or criteria for determining it; the existence of data subject rights (access, rectification, erasure, restriction, portability, objection); the right to withdraw consent at any time (where consent is the legal basis); the right to lodge a complaint with a supervisory authority; whether providing data is a statutory or contractual requirement and consequences of failure to provide; and the existence of automated decision-making including profiling with meaningful information about the logic and significance.
test_cases.supporting_quote: the controller shall, at the time when personal data are obtained, provide the data subject with the following further information necessary to ensure fair and transparent processing: (a) the period for which the personal data will be stored... (b) the existence of the right to request from the controller access to and rectification or erasure... (c) where the processing is based on point (a) of Article 6(1) or point (a) of Article 9(2), the existence of the right to withdraw consent... (d) the right to lodge a complaint with a supervisory authority... (e) whether the provision of personal data is a statutory or contractual requirement... (f) the existence of automated decision-making, including profiling

test_cases.question: If a company wants to use personal data for a new purpose different from the original collection purpose, what must they do?
test_cases.answer: Where the controller intends to further process the personal data for a purpose other than that for which the personal data were collected, the controller must provide the data subject prior to that further processing with information on that other purpose and with any relevant further information.
test_cases.supporting_quote: Where the controller intends to further process the personal data for a purpose other than that for which the personal data were collected, the controller shall provide the data subject prior to that further processing with information on that other purpose and with any relevant further information

test_cases.question: Must a controller still provide the required information at the time data are obtained if the data subject already has it?
test_cases.answer: No. Paragraphs 1, 2, and 3 of Article 13 do not apply where and insofar as the data subject already has the information. This prevents redundant disclosures when the individual is already aware of the required information.
test_cases.supporting_quote: Paragraphs 1, 2 and 3 shall not apply where and insofar as the data subject already has the information

coverage.13(1) timing: Test case 1 - At time when personal data are obtained
coverage.13(1) scope: Test case 2 - Only applies to direct collection (vs Article 14)
coverage.13(1)(a)(b): Test case 3 - Controller identity, representative, DPO contact details
coverage.13(1)(c)(d): Test case 4 - Purposes, legal basis, legitimate interests
coverage.13(1)(e): NOT EXPLICITLY COVERED - Recipients/categories (mentioned in TC6)
coverage.13(1)(f): Test case 5 - Third country transfers + safeguards
coverage.13(2): Test case 6 - NEW - Full additional info (retention, rights, consent withdrawal, complaints, statutory requirements, automated decisions)
coverage.13(3): Test case 7 - NEW - Must inform before processing for new purpose
coverage.13(4): Test case 8 - NEW - Exception when already has information

b2b_relevance: CRITICAL - Article 13 defines privacy notice requirements for direct data collection (e.g., sign-up forms, contact forms, purchases). Essential for: website privacy policies, app onboarding flows, customer registration, and employee data collection. Key takeaways: (1) Information must be provided AT TIME of collection, (2) Must inform about new purposes BEFORE using data for them, (3) No need to repeat if user already has the info.
